newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish '97 CPI goal within reach after March data.
newsitem.headline: Polish '97 CPI goal within reach after March data.

text.p: Poland's consumer price index fell to year-on-year 16.6 percent in March from 17.3 percent in February, putting the country's ambitious 13 percent target for December this year within reach, analysts said on Tuesday.
They said the overall index was pulled down by the slow growth of food prices, which rose 0.3 percent in March, to bring the year-on-year food price index down to 14.1 percent.

"Food prices have been pulling down the CPI index and the 13-percent goal has become realistic, with inflation below 14 percent in December very possible," Adam Czyzewski, economist at the independent NOBE economic institute.
Analysts expected slow food price growth to keep the overall index edging down for at least the next three months.

"I expect food prices will not rise more than 0.5 point each month in the next quarter, taking the year-on-year index below 16 percent already in April," said Taduesz Chroscicki, chief analyst at the government Centre for Strategic Studies.
Analysts said the 13 percent December target could be jeopardised if bad weather conditions damaged Poland's crops or fuel prices jumped on world markets.

They also said Poland needed to watch wage growth, which stood at more than four percent in real terms after the first quarter, against this year's budget target of a 2.5 percent real-term increase in 1997.
Poland is scheduled to hold parliamentary polls in the fourth quarter of the year.

Analysts said that although optimistic, the March data did not give sufficient grounds for a rate cut, as the National Bank of Poland and the finance ministry were more concerned with cooling the country's robust domestic demand.
